title: Cell E runtime: Ollama with the pinned small model on Ubuntu 24.04, CPU only
purpose: The required m23 runtime path for Cell E. Installs the dated v1 runtime as a system service, pulls the pinned small instruct model, proves first prompt, CPU residency, loopback, direct API, stop, and undo. Frozen fixture task: ticket classification (plan 06 amendment 3b-1). This cell trades speed for running anywhere, on purpose: same model, same commands, slower tokens, and the record says so instead of apologizing. Status is CANARY: authored 2026-07-25 from the verified Cell A record and the runtime's official documentation, not yet executed on this cell; it flips to current after a start-to-finish run on real Cell E hardware, at which point every expected output below gets replaced by the observed one.
hardware_class: Cell E: x86-64 CPU with 16 GB or more RAM
runtime_version: Install current from the official source; record the version this cell actually installs at verify; version drift is the first suspect if output differs (Cell A verified 0.20.2 on 2026-07-25)
prerequisites: sudo access; curl installed (sudo apt install -y curl if missing)
About 3 GB of free disk and a network connection for the one-time model pull
License reviewed: Qwen3.5-2B is Apache 2.0 (verify at the upstream repository); no remote code runs, GGUF weights only
estimated_download: 2.7 GB model artifact plus the runtime installer

steps.purpose: Download the official install script, read it, then run it. The read-before-run is Module 15's trust discipline: this script gets root.
steps.expected_output: After you quit the pager, the script installs the runtime, creates a systemd service, and starts it. On this cell it will report a CPU-only install; that is correct here, not a failure.
steps.stop: Ctrl+C during install; rerunning the script is safe.
steps.undo: sudo systemctl disable --now ollama stops and disables the service; the runtime's official documentation carries the full uninstall (binary, service unit, ollama user, and model store).
common_errors: curl: command not found: sudo apt install -y curl first.

steps.purpose: Record the exact runtime version and confirm the service is active.
steps.expected_output: A version string, then active. Cell A verified 0.20.2; record what this cell installs.
common_errors: inactive: sudo systemctl start ollama, then recheck.

steps.purpose: Pull the pinned small instruct model and record its digest.
steps.expected_output: Layer downloads then success; ollama list then shows qwen3.5:2b with ID 324d162be6ca and size 2.7 GB.
steps.stop: Ctrl+C is safe; rerunning the pull resumes or verifies.
steps.undo: ollama rm qwen3.5:2b removes the model; a later pull downloads it again.
common_errors: manifest unknown: check the exact model name and tag against the runtime's model library.

steps.purpose: First prompt. This model THINKS by default: the CLI streams its reasoning before the answer, and --hidethinking shows the answer alone. On CPU the reasoning tokens cost real seconds, which makes the thinking-off API options below matter even more on this cell.
steps.command: ollama run qwen3.5:2b --hidethinking "In one sentence, what is a context window?"
steps.expected_output: One short definition sentence. Cold start pauses while weights load into RAM; warm responses arrive at CPU pace, slower than the GPU cells and still entirely usable for short structured tasks. Record cold and warm timings at verify.
steps.stop: The one-shot form exits by itself; in interactive mode, /bye exits.
steps.undo: Nothing to undo; a prompt changes no state.
common_errors: Long pause before output: the model is loading into RAM (cold start) or thinking; both are normal and longer on CPU.

Empty content when calling the OpenAI-compatible API with a max_tokens cap: the thinking consumed the whole budget. Send reasoning_effort none on /v1/chat/completions, or think false on the native /api/chat route.

steps.purpose: Verify where the model actually runs; on this cell the honest answer is the CPU, and the record proves it rather than assuming it.
steps.expected_output: A row for qwen3.5:2b whose PROCESSOR column reports 100% CPU. That is correct for this cell, and it is the number that explains the pace of the previous step.
steps.stop: Nothing to stop; ps reads state.
common_errors: Empty list: the model unloaded after idling; run a prompt and check again.

steps.purpose: Confirm the service binds loopback only. The documented default bind is 127.0.0.1:11434; anything else means an OLLAMA_HOST override, usually via a systemd drop-in.
steps.expected_output: One listener on 127.0.0.1:11434. A 0.0.0.0:11434 or [::]:11434 line means the service listens on EVERY interface: treat that as the m23-6 exposure drill, find the override (systemctl cat ollama shows drop-ins), and decide on purpose.
steps.stop: Nothing to stop; ss reads state.
common_errors: No output: the service is not running; start it and retry.

steps.purpose: Prove the HTTP surface with a direct request before any application code.
steps.expected_output: A JSON model list whose data array includes an entry with id qwen3.5:2b.
steps.stop: Nothing to stop; the request returns immediately.
steps.undo: Nothing to undo; a GET changes no state.
common_errors: Connection refused: the service is stopped; start it and retry.

steps.purpose: Practice a clean stop and restart of a serve process you own, without touching the system service: run a second instance on loopback at another port, verify its bind, then stop it.
steps.expected_output: The serve process logs startup and stays attached; in a second terminal, ss -ltnp | grep 11500 shows 127.0.0.1:11500 only, and curl -s http://127.0.0.1:11500/api/version answers. Ctrl+C stops it cleanly.
common_errors: bind: address already in use: pick another free port for the drill.

The drill instance lists no models: expected. The system service runs as its own user with its own model store; your user-run instance has a separate one. The drill is about binds and lifecycle, and the port and process are real either way.

steps.purpose: Unload the model from memory when finished; the artifact stays on disk.
steps.expected_output: No output; ollama ps no longer lists the model, and RAM is released.
steps.undo: The next prompt reloads it automatically.

health_check: ollama --version answers, systemctl is-active ollama says active, ollama ps shows 100% CPU while loaded, ss shows the loopback listener, and the /v1/models request lists qwen3.5:2b
expected_result: DESK EXPECTATION pending on-OS verify: the pinned model pulls with the recorded digest, answers a first prompt at CPU pace, serves loopback HTTP, and stops cleanly. Forced-CPU datapoint 2026-07-27 (a GPU-equipped Ubuntu 24.04 box, a Zen 3 laptop CPU, 64 GB RAM, runtime 0.32.4, CPU load forced per-request with num_gpu 0, so NOT a real CPU-only cell run): course-scaffold smoke (the shipped m2 structured-output-classifier template instantiated with the frozen fixture schema) went 10 of 10 first-pass valid against every TicketClassification enum with classifications identical to the same box's GPU pass at temperature 0; ollama ps reported 100% CPU at 4096 context; warm responses averaged 6.4 s at about 19 tok/s versus 0.83 s at about 140 tok/s on GPU. Decoding held exactly as expected, only slower. Record this cell's own numbers at a real CPU-only verify.
expected_memory: DESK ESTIMATE pending on-OS verify: roughly 4 GB of system RAM for weights plus KV cache at 4096 context, comfortable inside the 16 GB floor; replace with the observed number
validated_context: 4096, course-validated on Cell A; revalidate on this cell at verify
privacy_notes: The tested path needs no account and no API key.
Documented default bind is loopback; the bind step verifies YOUR machine instead of trusting the default, and a wildcard bind is treated as the exposure drill.
The install script and the one-time model pull are the only network use in this recipe; prompts run locally.
This recipe proves the declared path on the tested date, not universal privacy for every plugin, setting, or future version.
known_failures: Thinking consumes a capped token budget on the OpenAI-compatible route, returning empty content: send reasoning_effort none there, or think false on the native route; on CPU the wasted thinking seconds hurt twice.
A machine near the 16 GB floor with heavy applications open can swap during load; close the heavy applications or drop a model size per the fit rule.
Cold starts pause longer than on the GPU cells while weights load; not a hang.
OLLAMA_HOST set in a systemd drop-in changes the bind; the bind step and systemctl cat ollama catch it.
